layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Accurate and efficient pixel-level crack detection is essential for infrastructure health monitoring. Although

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recent encoder-decoder architectures have achieved notable results, their reliance on aggressive downsampling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: often compromises the measurement-grade spatial precision required for fine crack detection. To address this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gap, we present HACNetV2, an enhanced full-resolution architecture that builds upon our previous HACNet.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Through key architectural refinements and novel components, HACNetV2 achieves substantially improved ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ficiency and effectiveness compared to its predecessor. HACNetV2 employs a dual-branch structure that in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tegrates full-resolution and high-resolution processing to maintain critical spatial detail without imposing a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heavy computational burden. Additionally, we propose two novel components: the hybrid atrous spatial pyramid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attention module (HybridASPA), which expands the receptive field while reducing computational complexity,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the crack-aware attention module (CrackAM), which enhances sensitivity to fine and complex crack features.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Together, these components enable HACNetV2 to enhance feature representation effectively. The experimental

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results on the public BCL and CHCrack5K benchmark datasets demonstrate that HACNetV2 outperforms recent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models, achieving superior mIoU and F1 scores while maintaining a lightweight structure with only 0.52 M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters. Furthermore, HACNetV2 supports real-time inference capabilities, processing 480 × 480 images at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 47 FPS on an RTX 3090 GPU.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The rapid development of global infrastructure, including tunnels,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bridges, and pavements, has led to an ever-growing demand for effective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maintenance solutions. Early identification and repair of defects are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crucial for prolonging the lifespan of these structures while ensuring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: public safety. Among various structural defects, cracks are the most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: common and pose significant challenges for manual inspection because

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of their time-consuming and labor-intensive nature (Dorafshan &

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Maguire, 2018; Schnebele et al., 2015). Consequently, automatic crack

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection has become a focal point for research.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Digital camera-based systems are particularly attractive due to their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low cost, flexibility in deployment, and ease of integration with existing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: measurement setups, ranging from handheld devices to robotic or drone-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mounted inspection units. However, achieving accurate pixel-level

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack detection still presents several challenges. First, cracks exhibit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distinct characteristics depending on the material (e.g., concrete,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: asphalt, steel) and the surface texture, which can complicate detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Tsai & Chatterjee, 2017). Secondly, variations in lighting, such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shadows, reflections, and glare, further hinder crack visibility, poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tially leading to false positives or missed detections (Ranyal et al., 2024).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Moreover; this issue is further complicated by the requirement that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: measured crack dimensions must be correlated with engineering stan-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dards and guidelines, such as those indicating that cracks wider than 0.2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mm may be safety-critical (Abou-Zeid et al., 2001; Toniolo & Di Prisco,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the past decade, deep learning approaches have shown strong

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature representation capabilities. Consequently, numerous convolu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional neural network (CNN)-based crack segmentation networks have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been proposed. Early CNN methods typically relied on patch-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: classification (Makantasis et al., 2015). In this paradigm, individual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: patches are classified as 'crack' or 'non-crack' (background). To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generate a refined crack mask, post-processing steps such as adaptive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thresholding (Zhang et al., 2018) and connectivity analysis (Loupos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2018) are commonly applied. This patch-based strategy is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computationally costly and lacks global context, which motivated the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subsequent development and adoption of end-to-end networks. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: networks typically employ an encoder-decoder architecture (Ai et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2023); as illustrated in Fig. 1(a), which includes two main modules: an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoder and a decoder. The encoder expands the receptive field and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extracts rich features through progressive downsampling, whereas the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder reconstructs spatial details for precise pixel-level segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The conventional encoder-decoder architecture may face segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: errors, particularly with fine and low-contrast cracks. This is due to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spatial resolution loss in the encoding stage and limited capacity to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recover this information during decoding, even with techniques such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: skip connections (Ronneberger et al., 2015) or max pooling index

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Badrinarayanan et al., 2017) reuse. To increase accuracy, some re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: searchers have proposed deeper CNN architectures (Yang et al., 2019) or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sophisticated multiscale methods (Zou et al., 2018). However, these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approaches often lead to larger and more complex models, which can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenging to deploy on resource-constrained measurement in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: struments used in field applications.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dilated convolutions have been proven effective in replacing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (b) HACNet

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (C) HACNetV2 (Ours)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1. Schematic comparison of the encoder-decoder networks, HACNet, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HACNetV2. Unlike the encoder-decoder architecture, HACNet avoids down-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sampling operations that reduce the data resolution. In HACNetV2, two sepa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rate resolution branches, combined with a simple CrackAM mechanism, are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduced to enhance model performance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: downsampling for expanding the receptive field without compromising

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature map resolution (Pelt & Sethian, 2018; Yu & Koltun, 2016). By

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: employing dilated convolutions, a full-resolution network with an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extensive receptive field can be constructed, alleviating spatial resolu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion loss in crack detection. However, research exploring this avenue

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: remains limited. Our previous work, the hybrid atrous convolutional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network (HACNet) (Chen & Lin, 2021); follows a similar philosophy. As

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: illustrated in Fig. 1(b), it avoids conventional downsampling and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: upsampling by using hybrid connected atrous convolutions to expand

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the receptive field, making it well-suited for detecting fine cracks in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: small-scale training sets. It has been benchmarked against other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods in various studies (Bai et al., 2024; Yang et al., 2023; Zhang &

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Liu, 2024). However, it faces limitations in computational efficiency,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: primarily because the processing of entire feature maps at full resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires more computational resources than downsampling-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods. Furthermore, by avoiding downsampling, it is unable to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectively model channel-wise feature dependencies, thereby con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: straining its overall feature representation capacity. These limitations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: restrict the construction of deeper and more powerful network archi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tectures, thus hindering its effectiveness in achieving high precision on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large-scale datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This presents a critical challenge: how can full-resolution network be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accelerated while improving its performance across various crack

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection scenarios? In this study, we address this issue by building upon

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HACNet as our baseline. Our preliminary experiments indicated that not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all crack features require computationally expensive full-resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolution operations. To optimize this, we reduce the number of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: channels in its high-resolution structure to lower computational costs. A

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high-resolution branch at half the original image scale is then intro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duced to enhance feature representation, thereby improving both the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accuracy and speed of crack detection. Additionally, recognizing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: success of attention mechanisms in computer vision, we revisited

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: existing channel attention mechanisms for crack detection. Our analysis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: revealed that some attention mechanisms originally designed for natural

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semantic scenes may be suboptimal for fine crack detection, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aligns with earlier studies (Lan & Dong, 2022; Sun et al., 2024). In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: natural semantic images, key features are densely distributed, allowing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attention mechanisms to focus on multiple regions with rich informa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion. In contrast, crack images typically contain sparse, elongated fea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures, with most of the image area being background. On the basis of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these observations, we propose a crack-aware attention module, named

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CrackAM, to ensure that both fine and coarse cracks receive appropriate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attention. We also introduce the effective hybrid atrous spatial pyramid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attention (HybridASPA), which integrates CrackAM to enable efficient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multiscale feature aggregation. Our final built model, HACNetV2 (see

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1(c)), achieves an improved balance between accuracy and speed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The key contributions of this work are summarized as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) We propose HACNetV2, a novel and efficient full-resolution crack

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection network. It employs a dual-branch structure that in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tegrates full-resolution and high-resolution processing, preser-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ving critical spatial details while maintaining computational

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: efficiency. Our results reaffirm that full-resolution networks can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strike a balance between computational efficiency and segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation performance in crack detection.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (2) We propose CrackAM, a simple yet effective attention module

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specifically designed for crack segmentation. CrackAM employs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: channel attention to recalibrate feature responses across chan-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nels, emphasizing both fine and elongated crack details. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lightweight, hyperparameter-free module can be seamlessly in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tegrated into crack detection networks as an add-on to improve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation quality.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (3) HACNetV2 features a simple and straightforward architecture,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with each HybridASPA block sharing the same structure, pa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rameters, input/output channels, and resolution. The model is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scalable, with increased channel capacity enhancing crack

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Related work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We briefly review existing model architectures relevant to our pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: posed method.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1. Encoder-decoder networks for crack detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Three classic encoder-decoder architectures—FCN (Long et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2015), U-Net (Ronneberger et al., 2015), and SegNet (Badrinarayanan

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2017)—have demonstrated strong performance in pixel-level

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack detection (Huang et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2019). Subsequent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: research has focused on enhancing these architectures. One approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: involves leveraging more powerful encoder backbones, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ResNet variants (Bang et al., 2019) and Vision Transformers (ViT) (Liu

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2023), to improve feature extraction capabilities. Another critical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strategy focuses on multi-scale feature fusion to capture contextual in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formation across different resolutions. Techniques such as spatial pyr-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amid pooling (SPP) (Gu et al., 2023) and the explicit fusion of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hierarchical convolutional features (Wang and Su, 2022) are commonly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: employed. For instance, Liu et al. (2019) proposed a DeepCrack network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adapting the FCN architecture with guided filters (He et al., 2013), while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Zou et al. (2018) introduced a distinct model, also termed DeepCrack,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: built upon SegNet, which specifically fuses features from corresponding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoder and decoder stages across scales.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The prediction speed is also critical for practical engineering appli-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cations in crack detection. Previous studies have focused on speeding up

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoder-decoder networks. For example, Chen et al. (2019) proposed a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learnable automatic switch module (SWM) that selectively bypasses the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder on the basis of the input image class, reducing computation by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 31 %–87 % without sacrificing accuracy. Choi and Cha (2020) improved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the speed by replacing standard convolutions with separable convolu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions and using fewer channels. Li et al. (2023) introduced HrSegNet, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: real-time, high-resolution crack detection network incorporating se-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mantic guidance; its HrSegNet-B32 variant achieves real-time inference

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while preserving fine crack details. Most recently, CarNet (Li et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2024) introduced an olive-shaped encoder and a lightweight multiscale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder to improve detection performance and computational

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: efficiency.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.2. Full-resolution segmentation networks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recent studies (Pelt and Sethian, 2018; Wang et al., 2018; Yu and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Koltun, 2016) have shown that CNNs without downsampling layers can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectively capture semantic information for segmentation tasks. Yu and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Koltun (2016) introduced dilated convolutions to aggregate multiscale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contextual information while preserving resolution. Varying dilation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rates allow feature capture at multiple scales, but their model suffers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from grid artifacts (Wang et al., 2018). To alleviate these gridding ar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tifacts, Hamaguchi et al. (2018) proposed a local feature extraction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (LFE) network with dilation rates that increase and then decrease,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yielding strong results in remote sensing imagery. However, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cascading atrous layers in this approach may struggle with long, narrow

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: objects like cracks. Pelt and Sethian (2018) developed a mixed-scale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dense network that combines dense connectivity with multiscale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature extraction, demonstrating improved accuracy and robustness in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image analysis.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In crack detection, few studies have focused on segmentation net-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: works without downsampling. An early instance is CrackNet (Zhang

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2017), which aims for pixel-level accuracy by merging convolu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional outputs with fully connected layers, but these layers are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameter-heavy and computationally intensive. CrackNet-V (Fei et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2020) improved this by replacing the fully connected layers with 3 × 3

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolutions and deepened the network. Despite this improvement, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: authors noted that small filters across layers struggled to represent a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large receptive field, resulting in a loss of spatial information in wide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cracks. HACNet (Chen and Lin, 2021) utilizes atrous convolutions with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exponentially increasing dilation rates to expand the receptive field and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a hybrid connection to aggregate multi-level features. Although these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approaches achieve high accuracy, they increase computational de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mands and latency, making real-time performance a challenge for full-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution architectures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.3. Attention modules in crack detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Attention mechanisms have become a key component of modern

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deep learning, helping models focus on relevant features while ignoring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: irrelevant data. Inspired by their success in general vision tasks,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attention-based methods have been adapted for crack detection (Ranyal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2024). Liu et al. (2019) incorporated the SE attention module (Hu

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2018) to optimize multi-dilation features. Wang et al. (2024) used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a coordinate attention module (Hou et al., 2021) to enhance the model's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perception of various spatial information. Qu and Wang (2023) intro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duced the gating attention unit (Oktay, 2018) to reduce background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: noise and improve crack localization. Tiny-Crack-Net (Chu et al., 2022)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explores the use of channel and spatial attention modules (Woo et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2018) to capture spatial relationships and contextual information for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack detection. CrackFormer (Liu et al., 2023) is a transformer-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoder-decoder structure that uses a combination of multiple local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: self-attention modules and scaling-attention modules to capture fine-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grained crack features.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, crack detection differs significantly from natural image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks (Chen et al., 2021). Cracks typically occupy a small portion of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image, unlike natural scenes where objects, textures, and features are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more evenly distributed across the frame. Considering these distinctions,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we rethink the channel attention mechanism in this work and propose a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack-aware attention module specifically tailored to the unique char-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: acteristics of crack images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Proposed approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1. Network architecture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1.1. Revisiting HACNet

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HACNet is a fully convolutional neural network designed to maintain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: full-resolution throughout its structure, ensuring fine-grained spatial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information for crack segmentation. It comprises an input layer, two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HybridASPPs, and an output head, sequentially. HybridASPP is a block

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of hybrid connected atrous convolutional layers that has a large recep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tive field. The output head consolidates the outputs from the Hybrid-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ASPPs to generate the final prediction map. HACNet has the advantages

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a simple structure and fewer parameters but does not adequately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: address computational inefficiency and limited feature representation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The reasons are as follows: (1) performing all convolution operations on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: full-resolution features results in high computational cost; (2) HACNet

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lacks the ability to effectively model channel-wise feature dependencies,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which compromises discriminative feature representation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1.2. The proposed HACNetV2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The simplest method to reduce the computational cost of full-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution networks is to decrease the number of internal channels or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lower the input resolution. However, the former weakens feature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the model's ability to restore spatial resolution. To resolve this, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: propose HACNetV2, which combines a small-channel full-resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branch with a high-resolution branch that operates at half the original

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image resolution. These two branches work in parallel, with their out-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flexibility makes HACNetV2 a versatile solution for a wide range of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: practical applications, accommodating diverse measurement scenarios

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and resource-limited environments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Compared with the SE modules used in crack detection models,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CrackAM offers two primary advantages: (1) an improved squeeze

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: module that ensures that both fine and coarse cracks receive adequate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attention, and (2) lower computational complexity with no hyper-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters, enhancing efficiency. Thus, CrackAM can be seamlessly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: integrated into both the full-resolution and high-resolution branches of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HACNetV2, enhancing crack detection performance across multiple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolutions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.4. Loss function

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Since most pixels in the images are non-crack (background), we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adopt the same loss function as HACNet, combining binary cross-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entropy and Dice loss for training. For more details, please refer to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HACNet paper (Chen & Lin, 2021). HACNetV2 has three side-output

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layers and one fused prediction layer; as shown in Fig. 2. We imple-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment a multi-layer supervision strategy (Lee et al., 2015); applying the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: overall loss to each output individually. This enables more robust opti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mization and ensures that the model can effectively handle the varied

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outputs from the different branches.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. Experiments and results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.1. Datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Numerous public crack datasets exist, but most are relatively small in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scale and quantity compared with general datasets (Pandey and Achara,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2024); such as ADE20K (Zhou et al., 2017), making it difficult to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: establish a fair benchmark for algorithm comparison. Furthermore,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cracks exhibit different characteristics on various materials, such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concrete and asphalt, and are also influenced by the capturing equip-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment. To create a more realistic engineering application scenario, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: promising approach is to combine these smaller datasets into a larger,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comprehensive dataset. Therefore, in this experiment, we use two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 4.2. Evaluation metrics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Crack detection is a binary semantic segmentation task in which the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: goal is to separate cracks (foreground) from non-cracks (background). A

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: threshold of 0.5 is applied to the network's probability map output to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generate a binary crack map. The performance is evaluated via four

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: common metrics: precision (P), recall (R), the F1score, and the mean

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intersection over union (mIoU). The formulas for these metrics are as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where TP, FP, TN, and FN are true positives, false positives, true nega-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tives, and false negatives, respectively. mIoU is the average IoU of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background and foreground segments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Model speed is crucial for practical use. Latency is measured in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frames per second (FPS) by averaging the processing time for all test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images with a batch size of one on a single RTX 3090 GPU. Giga floating-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: point operations (GFLOPs) and parameters (Params) are used to assess

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computational complexity and model size.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.3. Experimental settings

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The experiments are conducted on a workstation equipped with two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Nvidia RTX 3090 GPUs, 48 GB of RAM, and an Intel E5-2620v4 CPU.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HACNetV2 is implemented in Python using the PyTorch deep learning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: framework and runs on the Ubuntu 20.04 operating system. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: simplicity, we use random flipping as the sole data augmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method, avoiding more complex techniques such as cropping. HAC-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NetV2 is trained from scratch using the "He normal" initialization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method (He et al., 2015), without pre-trained weights. The initial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning rate is set at 0.0004, and it is reduced by 20 % every 30 epochs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Training uses the Adam optimizer (Kingma and Ba, 2014) with a mini-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: batch size of 12, following a consistent schedule across both datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Training ends after 150 epochs, and the best-performing model on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: validation set is selected for testing.

layout_dets.text: 4.4. Ablation study

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To evaluate the effectiveness of each component in HACNetV2, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conduct an ablation study on the BCL dataset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.4.1. Effectiveness of two branches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In HACNetV2, the incorporation of features from the two branches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: functions similarly to an ensemble model, but it is more straightforward

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and efficient. To evaluate the impact of combining these branches, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: then use only the high-resolution (HR) branch, which operates at half

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the original image resolution. Finally, we test two ensemble methods:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one that involves training the two branches independently and aver-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aging their outputs, and another that uses the HACNetV2 architecture,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which integrates features from both branches under full end-to-end

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (E2E) training. The models are trained under consistent experimental

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions. Table 2 summarizes the results, where HACNet-FR and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by averaging outputs. The results indicate that the E2E ensemble

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training of HACNetV2 achieves an mIoU of 82.39 %, which is 0.98 %,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.49 %, and 0.64 % higher than those of the models using the FR and HR

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branches individually, as well as the Ens_Indep method, respectively.

layout_dets.text: 4.6. Discussion on inference efficiency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The top portion of Table 4 focuses on lightweight, low-latency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models tested on the BCL and CHCrack5K datasets. Using only the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high-resolution branch, HACNetV2-HR achieves the best performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: among all the compared methods, including HrSegNetB32, Liu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DeepCrack, and CarNet, reaching an mIoU of 80.90 % on the BCL test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set at 492 FPS. Compared with other lightweight networks, HACNetV2-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HR also achieves superior results on CHCrack5K. HACNetV2 has the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowest FLOPs compared with the other methods listed in the bottom

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: section of Table

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indicating higher computational efficiency. Despite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: U-Net's FLOPS being significantly higher than that of HACNetV2, its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inference speed is faster. This is because FLOPS does not directly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correlate with the actual inference speed (Ma et al., 2018). A model with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fewer FLOPS can exhibit higher inference latency due to inefficiencies in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: memory usage, lack of hardware optimization, or architectural features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that hinder parallel execution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Through inference efficiency analysis, we find that HACNetV2 is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: highly scalable. The lightweight model HACNetV2-HR is compact and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: efficient while maintaining competitive performance, making it well

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: suited for real-time applications. Moreover, HACNetV2, a medium-sized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model, delivers state-of-the-art results on both datasets, highlighting the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectiveness and efficiency of our network architecture. HACNetV2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processes 480 × 480 images at real-time speeds, achieving 47 FPS on a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: single RTX 3090, which is slightly faster than HACNet-D, with improved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack detection accuracy. By increasing the channel capacity to 48 in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HACNetV2-W, the segmentation accuracy improves by 0.98 % on BCL

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 0.24 % on CHCrack5K compared to the baseline HACNetV2. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhancement makes the model suitable for applications requiring high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection accuracy, despite the increase in parameters and computa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional complexity.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.7. Analysis of limitations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Despite its strengths, HACNetV2 encounters challenges when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detecting extremely fine cracks, particularly in images with complex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: backgrounds. Fig. 9 (highlighted in yellow boxes) illustrates several

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: failure cases, where shallow cracks, thin cracks, and cracks against

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intricate backgrounds (e.g., stains) are not accurately segmented. Red

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boxes indicate false positives, such as over-segmentation errors

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: involving the edges of manhole covers and other structural elements.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These limitations may be due to the limited representation of such cases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the training dataset, leading to an imbalance that impacts the learning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process. Furthermore, current deep learning models, including HAC-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NetV2, still face difficulties in generalizing to cracks of varying shapes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within complex backgrounds that have limited visual cues. We believe

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that the accuracy and robustness of HACNetV2 could be further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhanced by (1) expanding the training dataset with more diverse

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labeled examples and (2) developing larger and deeper model archi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tectures to enhance feature representation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.8. Results on real application

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To verify the practical applicability of HACNetV2 without additional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adjustments, we develop a simple, real-time crack detection device (see

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 10(a)). This system comprises a professional SONY ILX-LR1 camera

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equipped with a 40-mm SONY lens, a Jetson Orin AGX edge device, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an LCD touchscreen display for immediate visualization of detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results. We train the model on the entire CHCrack5K dataset, convert it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into a TensorRT format, and deploy it on the Jetson Orin AGX platform.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The ILX-LR1 captures real-time video streams at a resolution of 3840 ×

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2160. To accommodate computational constraints, each frame is center-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cropped and resized to 480 × 480 pixels before processing with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HACNetV2.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We conduct experiments on pavement roads in Hangzhou, China, to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assess the model's performance under real-world conditions. As shown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Fig. 10(b), HACNetV2 successfully detects cracks in diverse and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenging scenarios, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: practical, on-site deployment. Furthermore, the model achieves an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inference speed of approximately 41 ms per image (~24 FPS) on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Jetson Orin AGX, ensuring near real-time performance. These results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: highlight HACNetV2's suitability for deployment on embedded plat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forms and IoT devices where computational and energy resources may

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be constrained.
